scope.c08: Advisory whole-function scalar expression helpers; builtin u32 operators, ordered formal roles and literal holes only. At least two builtin operations in each supported body. No rewrite or total-equivalence claim.
scope.c09: Synthetic lifecycle of independently specified findings; review identity is separate from report-local function handles.
scope.evidence: Source-authored labels, not copied from producer output. These embedded sources are specifications, not newly captured compiler evidence.

required_correspondence: first formal maps to first formal independently of binder spelling
outer multiplication maps to outer multiplication with ordered operands
inner addition maps to inner addition with ordered operands
literal 1 versus 3 is a parameter hole at the second operand of inner addition
literal 2 is common and remains common
required_limitations: proposal is not an automatic safe rewrite

sources: pub fn first(value: u32, mask: u32) -> u32 { (value ^ mask) & 15 }
pub fn second(input: u32, bits: u32) -> u32 { (input ^ bits) & 15 }
required_correspondence: ordered xor then and computation is retained

sources: pub fn first(value: u32) -> u32 { value }
pub fn second(input: u32) -> u32 { input }
proposal_cases.reason: Identity forwarding contains no useful repeated computation. Structural similarity alone is insufficient.

sources: pub fn first(value: u32) -> u32 { value + 1 }
pub fn second(input: u32) -> u32 { input + 3 }
proposal_cases.reason: Literal correspondence is possible, but this deliberately bounded consumer requires at least two builtin operations per member.

sources: pub fn first(left: u32, right: u32) -> u32 { (left - right) * 2 }
pub fn second(left: u32, right: u32) -> u32 { (right - left) * 2 }
proposal_cases.reason: Subtraction operands refer to opposite formal positions. This consumer cannot silently permute formal arguments or align operands by unordered labels.

counterexample.observation: first subtraction yields 5; second subtraction underflows with checked arithmetic, and differs with wrapping arithmetic

sources: pub fn first(value: u32, callback: fn(u32) -> u32) -> u32 { (callback(value) + 1) * 2 }
pub fn second(input: u32, callback: fn(u32) -> u32) -> u32 { (callback(input) + 3) * 2 }
proposal_cases.reason: Unknown callable behavior has no bounded summary; two visible builtin operations do not establish a supported complete expression.
required_invariants: opaque call is retained as a reason
no proposal over a stripped remainder

sources: pub fn first(value: u32, state: &mut u32) -> u32 { *state = value; (value + 1) * 2 }
pub fn second(input: u32, state: &mut u32) -> u32 { *state = input; (input + 3) * 2 }
proposal_cases.reason: The bounded scalar-expression consumer does not cover mutation or shared state; body writes cannot disappear from the proposed abstraction.

required_invariants: connected pair edges are not all-pair proof
every proposed member pair requires independent correspondence
group policy cannot be silently widened

review_identity_contract.hash_policy: Prefer scoped IDs/exact equality; if persisted byte fingerprints are needed use existing XXH3-64 convention, never new SHA. Do not serialize JSON solely to hash a run-local ID.
review_identity_contract.exact_equality: Retain and compare full versioned locator/context and relevant finding/member structure; a matching hash is not semantic identity or authority.

invariants: same full locator/context and relevant structure
same locator alone cannot conceal relevant operation change
preserve old review reason for inspection
source equality does not merge different compilation contexts
short names alone do not identify review entries
duplicate/unresolved declaration discriminators are ambiguous, not merged
inject colliding fingerprint in tests without requiring real XXH3 collision
dismissal lookup compares full exact key
membership growth changes exact finding identity
new member has complete independently checked pair correspondence
growth retention requires explicit recorded user choice
new member independently valid under the unchanged proposal policy
allow-growth does not authorize losing or reshaping reviewed members
version/policy changes cannot silently inherit dismissal
compatibility migration requires named tested contract

delivery_gate: Execute positive/negative cases against the implemented consumer, retaining explicit not-evaluated and unsupported outcomes.
Verify exact-key collision isolation and each review transition with implementation tests.
Do not call these capabilities delivered merely because this acceptance file exists.
